stages.does: take a source film from the archive, with who paid for it and why
cut the film into shots where the picture changes
stages.tool: the archive's own shot pass (named in each clip's path)

stages.does: write each of the 45 signs as one question and a test that tells it from its neighbours
turn each question into scene phrases and run them on the archive's shot search
take the archive's thumbnail: the one frame every machine looks at
turn the frame into 512 numbers, then lay every shot out so close numbers sit close: the picture map
score the frame against 20 subjects and 5 shot scales
write one plain sentence of what the frame shows
measure loudness and whether it is speech, music or silence
turn the sound into numbers, name it from 30 everyday sounds, and lay the heard shots out by sound: the sound map
compare the frame with each sign's words and read examples; keep the 3 closest as places to look
write down every word spoken, with the second it is said
lay a sign's search results on a contact sheet; keep the shots that answer its question
write one sentence naming the sign and what in the frame answers its question
score the reading: how sure in context, how sure from the shot alone, which rival sign, what would flip it
find the second in the clip where the read frame sits
cut out the figure the reading is about and follow it frame by frame
place the shot in one of our films
